Sources

Standards and sources

Every claim in the academy traces to a source with a version and a review date. This is the register, including what is verified and what still needs rechecking.

Source register

Review date 2026-11-25. Verified means read in this review. Carried means kept from the research blueprint and rechecked before release.

Academic domains underpinning the curriculum

The academy integrates established computer-security disciplines with the newer research fields required to secure tool-using and autonomous systems.

Academic domainHow it informs the curriculum
Computer security foundationsSecurity properties, threat modelling, trust boundaries, attack surfaces, defence in depth and security economics.
Capability security and access controlLeast privilege, object capabilities, delegation, reference monitors, confused deputies and policy decision/enforcement separation.
Operating systems and isolationProcesses, namespaces, containers, virtual machines, sandboxing, filesystem controls, resource limits and kernel boundaries.
Distributed systems and fault tolerancePartial failure, retries, idempotency, consensus, timeouts, queues, circuit breakers and cascading agent actions.
Programming languages and secure softwareType systems, memory safety, taint tracking, secure APIs, dependency hygiene, secure SDLC and code review.
Formal methods and assuranceState machines, invariants, temporal properties, model checking, safety cases and assurance arguments.
Information-flow security and privacyNoninterference, data classification, provenance, retention, deletion, tenant isolation and controlled information release.
Cryptography and identity systemsAuthentication, workload identity, key management, signing, token exchange, sender-constrained tokens and revocation.
Machine learning and adversarial MLTraining-data integrity, poisoning, backdoors, model extraction, evasion, robustness and model lifecycle security.
LLM and agent architecturePlanning, tool use, orchestration, memory, retrieval, multi-agent coordination, context windows and action boundaries.
Natural-language and multimodal securityDirect and indirect prompt injection, untrusted instructions, image/audio/video payloads and context provenance.
Data engineering and retrieval systemsETL pipelines, vector stores, embeddings, retrieval filtering, index integrity, data lineage and RAG authorisation.
Cloud-native, network and platform securityNetwork segmentation, egress policy, secrets, cloud IAM, inference endpoints, workload isolation and shared responsibility.
Software and model supply-chain securitySBOM/ML-BOM, provenance, registries, signing, dependency confusion, build integrity, model artefacts and rollback.
Security operations and digital forensicsTelemetry, detection engineering, incident command, evidence preservation, event reconstruction, containment and recovery.
Safety engineering and resilienceHazard analysis, STPA, human factors, fail-safe design, operational technology boundaries and service continuity.
HCI and cognitive scienceAutomation bias, trust calibration, approval fatigue, explainability, interface design and human-agent coordination.
Privacy, law, governance and organisational riskAI governance, accountability, regulatory mapping, procurement, supplier assurance, risk appetite and audit.
Empirical research and measurementBenchmark validity, adaptive evaluation, attack success, false positives, utility preservation, reproducibility and statistical interpretation.

Selected research literature and benchmarks

A curated starting set, not an exhaustive bibliography. Benchmarks are teaching and evaluation instruments; their limitations must be taught alongside their results.

ResearchVenueCurriculum contribution
AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM AgentsNeurIPS 2024Dynamic tool-use benchmark with 97 realistic tasks and 629 security test cases; teaches adaptive evaluation rather than static prompt examples.
InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated LLM AgentsFindings of ACL 20241,054 test cases across 17 user tools and 62 attacker tools; informs source/sink mapping, tool abuse and exfiltration exercises.
Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based AgentsICLR 2025Ten scenarios, 400+ tools, 27 attack/defence methods and seven metrics; highlights the need to measure utility alongside security.
AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM AgentsICLR 2025110 harmful agent tasks, 440 augmented variants and 11 harm categories; informs safe evaluation of multi-step agent misuse.
SEC-bench: Automated Benchmarking of LLM Agents on Real-World Software Security TasksNeurIPS 2025Reproducible vulnerability reproduction and patching tasks; teaches the difference between plausible remediation and demonstrated fixes.
AgentDyn: A Dynamic Open-Ended Benchmark for Evaluating Prompt Injection AttacksarXiv preprint, 202660 open-ended tasks and 560 injection cases; identifies weaknesses in static tasks and the risk of over-defence. Preprint status is retained.
Beyond Guardrails: Runtime Enforcement for Secure AI Agents — A Systematic ReviewJournal of Reliable and Secure Computing, 2026Review of 58 studies; supports independent runtime enforcement and identifies gaps in OS/process boundaries, delegation and standardised evaluation.
Vulnerabilities in Autonomous Execution: A Survey of Security Threats and Defenses in LLM-Driven Agentic and Multi-Agent SystemsKnowledge-Based Systems, 2026PRISMA-informed review of 44 attack papers; consolidates indirect injection, malicious tools, inter-agent infection and memory poisoning, and finds multi-agent propagation under-defended.
Tracing MCP Security Vulnerabilities: Constructing and Analyzing an MCP Security Vulnerability DatasetIEEE Security & Privacy Workshops 2026Initial paper snapshot validates 24 MCP vulnerabilities from 119 candidate records; injection and path traversal account for 66.7% of that frozen sample. Later dataset releases extend beyond the paper sample.
Argument-Aware Runtime Least-Privilege Enforcement Against Tool-Poisoning-Induced Actions in MCP-Based Agentic SystemsFuture Internet, 4 November 2026A bounded client-side capability-inference and policy-enforcement proof of concept. The paper explicitly limits generalisation; use it to motivate request-argument inspection, not as proof of universal interception.
Cryptographically Verifiable Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents: A Falsifiable Hypothesis and Proof of ConceptFrontiers in Computer Science, 24 September 2026A hypothesis-and-theory article with a zero-knowledge proof of concept; formalises request-, principal-, context- and policy-binding. It remains preliminary and has not evaluated multi-agent delegation chains.

How we use sources

  • Teach the concept in our own words. Cite requirement identifiers, not protected text.
  • Pin the version and the review date wherever a figure or a date appears.
  • Where sources disagree, say so and follow the primary source.
  • Standards change quickly. A scheduled scan and a change trigger update affected lessons, and the lesson changelog records it.
  • Paid standards are taught as concepts without reproducing protected text.

Reviewed 2026-11-25. Intellica is independent of GIAC, ISC2, ISACA, CompTIA, CSA, IAPP, OWASP, MITRE and NIST. Mappings show how our lessons relate to published objectives. They are not an affiliation, an approval or a prediction of any exam result.
